questions.question: In an election between two candidates, 8% of the votes were invalid. The winning candidate got 60% of the total valid votes and won the election by 5888 votes. How many voters were registered?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

8% of the votes are invalid

Winner got 60% of the valid votes

Winners won by 5888 votes

**Calculation:**

Let the total numbers of voters be 100a

Valid votes = 100a - 100a × 8%

⇒ 92a

Winning candidate got 92a × 60%

⇒ 55.2a

So, loosing candidate got = 92a - 55.2a

⇒ 36.8a

According to the question,

55.2a - 36.8a = 5888

⇒ 18.4a = 5888

⇒ a = 5888/18.4

⇒ a = 320

So, total voters registered = 320 × 100

⇒ 32000

**∴ 32000 voters were registered.**

questions.question: The average weight of X and Y is 40 kg. The average weight of Y and R is 62 kg and the average weight of X and R is 56 kg. The weight of X is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The average weight of X and Y is 40 kg

The average weight of Y and R is 62 kg

The average weight of X and R is 56 kg

**Concept used:**

Average = Sum of elements/Number of elements

**Calculation:**

Total of X and Y = 40 × 2 = 80 kg ----(i)

Total of Y and R = 62 × 2 = 124 kg ----(ii)

Total of X and R = 56 × 2 = 112 kg ----(iii)

By adding eq (i), (ii), and (iii) we get

2(X + Y + R) = 316

⇒ X + Y + R = 158 ----(iv)

From eq (ii) and eq (iv) we can say

X = 158 - 124

⇒ 34 kg

**∴ The weight of X is 34 kg.**

questions.question: A can finish as much work in 6 days as C can in 8 days. B can finish as much work in 6 days as C can in 4 days. How much time will B require to finish a work if A takes 54 days to finish it?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A can finish as much work in 6 days as C can in 8 days.

B can finish as much work in 6 days as C can in 4 days.

**Concept used:**

Total work = Efficiency of the worker × time taken by them

**Calculation:**

Let the efficiency of the A, B, and C be a, b, and c

According to the question,

6a = 8c

⇒ a/c = 8/6 = 4/3 ----(i)

Again,

6b = 4c

⇒ b/c = 4/6 = 2/3 ----(ii)

From eq (i) and eq (ii) we can say

a : b : c = 4 : 2 : 3

Let efficiency of them be 4x and 2x and 3x

Now,

Required work = 54 × 4x

⇒ 216x

Required time = 216x/2x

⇒ 108 days

**∴ B will require 108 days to finish a work if A takes 54 days to finish it.**

questions.question: The difference between the compound interest and the simple interest on a certain sum at 10% per annum for 2 years is ₹1,200. Find the sum.
questions.solution:
Given:

The difference between compound interest and simple interest on a certain sum at 10 percent per annum for 2 years is Rs. 1200.

Concept used:

Difference between compound interest and simple interest for 2 years:

Difference = P × (r/100)2

Here, P = principal or sum, r = Rate of interest

Calculation:

Let the sum be Rs. P

1200 = P × (10/100)2

⇒ 1200 = P × (1/10)2

⇒ 1200 = P/100

⇒ P = 1200 × 100 = Rs. 120000

**∴ The sum is Rs. 120000.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**

CI for 2 years at 10% = P(1 + r/100)² - P

⇒ CI = P[(1 + 10/100)² - 1]

⇒ CI = P[(11/10)² - 1]

⇒ CI = P(121 - 100)/100

⇒ CI = 21/100 × P

SI for 2 years at 10% = (P × 10 × 2)/100

⇒ SI = 20P/100

Now, CI - SI = 1200

21P/100 - 20P/100 = 1200

P/100 = 1200

P = 120000

**Hence, the sum is Rs. 120000.**

questions.question: A man buys milk at ₹50 per litre and adds to it water equal to one-third of the milk. If he sells it at ₹60 per litre, then find his profit percentage.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Cost of milk = 50/L

Selling price of mixture = 60/L

**Concept used:**

Seeling price = Cost price + profit

Profit% = (Profit/Cost price) × 100

**Calculation:**

Let the quantity of the milk in the mixture be 3x

So, the quantity of the water = 3x × (1/3)

⇒ x

Total cost of the mixture = (3x × 50) + x × 0 [As water has no value in money]

⇒ 150x

Now,

Selling price = 60(3x + x)

⇒ 60 × 4x

⇒ 240x

Profit = 240x - 150x

⇒ 90x

Profit % = (90x/150x) × 100

⇒ 60

**∴ His profit percentage is 60%.**

questions.question: What is the largest 4-digit number that is divisible by 10, 15 and 18?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The number are 10, 15, and 18

**Concept used:**

We know that, If the number is divisible by given numbers then it should be the multiple of their LCM

**Calculation:**

LCM of 10, 15, and 18 = 90 

Now the largest 4-digit number is 9999

If we divide 9999 by 90 we get the remainder as 9

The number completely divisible by 10, 15, and 18 = 9999 - 9 

⇒ 9990 

**∴ The largest 4-digit number that is divisible by each of 10, 15, and 18 is 9990.**

questions.question: An AC can cool a hall in 10 min, while an AC of another brand can cool the same hall in 15 min. If both the ACs are switched on at the same time, then in how much time will they cool the hall?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

1st AC can cool in 10 min

2nd AC can cool in 15 min

**Concept used:**

Total work = Time taken by the objects to do a work × efficiency of the objects

**Calculation:**

LCM of 10 and 15 = 30 i.e total work

Now,

Efficiency of the 1st AC = 30/10 = 3 units/min

Efficiency of the 2nd AC = 30/15 = 2 units/min

Effective efficiency of the two ACs = 3 + 2 = 5 units/min

Time taken to cool the hall when two ACs are on together = 30/5

⇒ 6 min

**∴ They will cool the hall in 6 min.**

questions.question: At what rate of simple interest will a sum of ₹4,500 amount to ₹5,310 after 4 years?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Simple Interest for 4 years = ₹5,310 − ₹4,500 = ₹810

Simple Interest for 1 year = 810 ÷ 4 = ₹202.5

Rate % = (1-year Interest ÷ Principal) × 100

Rate % = (202.5 ÷ 4500) × 100 = 4.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 4.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹4,500

Amount (A) = ₹5,310

Time (T) = 4 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Amount (A) = P + SI

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3be056a4c94901609997a3b6a443ea095526f3af04a0530e97522e0040e0f9f0.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI = A − P

⇒ SI = 5310 − 4500 = ₹810

⇒ 810 = (4500 × R × 4) ÷ 100

⇒ 810 = 45 × R × 4

⇒ 810 = 180 × R

⇒ R = 810 ÷ 180

⇒ R = 4.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 4.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest

When interest is compounded annually, Amount A = P × (1 + R÷100)T.

SI vs CI Difference

For 2 years, the difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest on the same principal is P × (R÷100)².

Rule of 72

A simple rule to estimate the number of years required to double the invested money at a given annual interest rate (Time ≈ 72 ÷ R).

questions.question: A trader lists his articles 26% above the cost price and allows a discount of 15% on every article. What is his gain percentage?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A trader marked up his articles 25% more than the cost price.

He offered a discount of 10%

**Concept used:**

Selling price = Marked price × (100 – discount)%

Profit% = [(Selling price - Cost price)/Cost price] × 100

**Calculation:**

Let the cost price be 100a.

Marked price = 100a × 126%

⇒ 126a

Selling price = 126a × 85%

⇒ 107.1a

Profit% = [(107.1 - 100)/100] × 100

⇒ 7.1%

**∴ Trader’s gain percentage is 7.1**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__**

CP/MP = (100 - D%)/(100 + P%)

100/126 = (100 - 15)/(100 + P%)

100/126 = 85/(100 + P%)

(100 + P%) = 85 × 126/100

(100 + P%) = 17 × 63/10

(100 + P%) = 107.1 

P% = 7.1% 

**Hence, the correct answer is 7.1%**

questions.question: The letter B in the BODMAS rule stands for:
questions.solution:
Bodmas stands for

B - Brackets

O - Orders (powers/indices or roots)

D - Division

M - Multiplication

A - Addition

S - Subtraction

**∴ The letter B in the BODMAS rule stands for Brackets.**
